Messages.Author: SCALAR NORSE
Messages.Body:
If say i were to have already put out a milicint smith and it is now in
my preditor's preditor's possesion and bring out another milicint smith
now contesting with my old milicint which is no longer mine.

What happens if we both want to burn our contested cards?

Or i wanna burn mine before his?

Help would much be appreaciated.

Messages.Author: James R. McClure Jr.
Messages.Body:
wa...@nevada.edu (SCALAR NORSE) wrote:
>
>If say i were to have already put out a milicint smith and it is now in
>my preditor's preditor's possesion and bring out another milicint smith
>now contesting with my old milicint which is no longer mine.
>
>What happens if we both want to burn our contested cards?

Peace be with you,

The normal sequence of play takes care of this. You may only contest (pay one
pool) or yield (burn the card) a contested card during your Untap. Since you
must be playing the MS during your Master Phase, your Untap is already passed.
Unless you can somehow take another turn before your grand-pred, s/h/it will
have the first opportunity to burn the contested MS.

>Or i wanna burn mine before his?

You can't, due to the sequence of play (barring use of the two vote cards that
allow you to switch positions).

Nil carborundum illigitimi,

Since I'm too meticulous for my own good, I'll add another possibility:

If the First Tradition: Masquerade were in effect, and your Grand-predator
declines to pay the two-pool penalty (and skips this turn), then Your
Grand-predator would not be given the chance to contest or yield Milicent,
and you could do so on your turn (assuming you pay the two pool penalty
to take your turn if 1st Trad is still in effect at that time).
